_doc: Materials the native renderers draw with, by name (native/src/render/render_context.h); each params key is a uniform of its shader or of the files it includes, set by name (render/city_world.gd materials()), which the gates check (gate_materials.py). Colours as '#rrggbb', textures as res:// paths. prop lens_roughness and lens_ior: the signal lens, polished polycarbonate (Physically Based database, physicallybased.info, 'Plastic (PC)': roughness 0, index of refraction 1.5848 from refractiveindex.info). Vegetation wind (vegetation.gdshaderinc): wind_speed_ms 3 = Beaufort 2, light breeze 1.6-3.3 m/s (WMO); sway_per_ms2 = top bend per (m/s)^2 from Peltola et al. 1993 (crown-centre bending under 5 cm on a 13.5 m pine at 8 m/s: 0.0037 of the height, times (1/0.6)^2 to the top, over 64); gust_m = 22 x 10 m (Kaimal et al. 1972 spectral peak n z / U = 1/22); turbulence = 1 / ln(10 m / 0.05 m) (EN 1991-1-4 eq. 4.7, terrain category II); sway_hz = natural frequency of leafy trees of 8-15 m, 0.2-0.3 Hz (Jackson et al. 2019). wind_dir_x and wind_dir_z: a unit vector; the map has no geographic north, so no climate record applies to the way the wind blows. vegetation_cards cover_per_mip 0.25: alpha rescaled by mip level so a card keeps its coverage far away (Golus 2021, Anti-aliased Alpha Test: The Esoteric Alpha To Coverage). vegetation roughness 0.85: modelling choice for matte leaves, no published value. wire (wires.gdshader): a cable's own finish, metal 0.3 and roughness 0.55, as the reference game draws its wires (a dark cable with a sheen), apart from the furniture's matte 0.85, which lit a wire from the sky to the asphalt's own tone by day; wire_clamp_px 1: a cable thinner than a pixel is drawn a pixel wide, the reference's least width with no multisampling (the reference also blends such a cable by the share it fills; blended, this game's wires drew nothing: problem in doc/problems.jsonl). Drawn at 0.7 px and matte, a wire was a fraction of a pixel in the asphalt's own tone: poles with no wires by day.

agent._doc: Vehicles. Lamp colours: head_glow a halogen headlamp bulb, a black body at 3200 K (Philips H4 standard bulb); tail_glow the corner of UNECE R48 §2.30 red (y <= 0.335, z <= 0.008: x 0.657, y 0.335); sign_glow the middle of R48 amber (0.398 <= y <= 0.429 on z = 0.007), each from CIE 1931 (Wyman, Sloan & Shirley 2013 fit) to sRGB, out-of-gamut parts clipped, the brightest channel at 1. brake_ratio: a stop lamp at least 5 times its rear position lamp (UNECE R7 §6.2.4.2). Roughness (physicallybased.info): paint 0 (Car Paint: clear topcoat), lens 0 for lamps, signs and the far level's glass (Plastic (PC), Glass), skin 0.5 (Skin I-VI), helmet 0 (Plastic (PC) shell), trim 0.7 (the database's tyre rubber) for every unpainted part, cloth 1 (a matte textile: the database has none). head_power, tail_power, sign_power: how bright the lit lamps draw, set on the night photo (05_traffic at 10_night): a lamp's brightest channel at the top of the display range without bleeding into its body. signal_hz, signal_duty: an indicator flashes 90 times a minute (Council Directive 93/92/EEC, annex, direction-indicator lamps, as a search of its copy at legislation.gov.uk/eudr/1993/92 shows it: 'the flashing frequency must be 90 ± 30 per minute'; the document itself did not open here), lit half of each flash (a choice); by day its colour is agents.json trim.signal_lit, by night sign_glow at the stop lamp's ratio. signal_least_px, signal_most_m: a lit indicator is drawn as a light point is, never under a least size on the screen (OpenGL Performer Programmer's Guide, chapter 21 'Light Points': 'The apparent size of a light point can only range between the minimum and maximum sizes', PFLPS_SIZE_MIN_PIXEL; OpenSceneGraph's osgSim::LightPointNode setMinPixelSize): its lens grows round its centre until its larger side covers signal_least_px pixels (4: a dot the eye finds on a 1080p picture, a choice), never larger than signal_most_m (0.6 m, a third of a car's width, a choice: from far the light does not cover its vehicle).

far_cars._doc: The far traffic's cars (far_cars.gdshader, render/agents/far_traffic.h): a hull in its paint, as rough as the near cars' trim; by night its two ends burn as the near cars' lamps do (head_glow and tail_glow, the agent's own values), lamp_share of its half length from each end. Choices, no source: body_roughness, lamp_share.

agent_glass._doc: Vehicle glass (agent_glass.gdshader): transmittance 0.70, the least a windscreen and the windows the driver needs may let through (CONTRAN Resolução 960/2022 art. 4º I); ior 1.52, soda-lime glass, roughness 0 (physicallybased.info Glass); tint the 4.0's cool grey-blue (#7896a2), no source behind it, at 40 % in linear light: this sun lights it more than the 4.0's, and at its own value the panes showed milky over a dark cabin (par-hatch-frente).

marks._doc: Decals on the depth buffer (marks.gdshader): lie_above_m, the most a surface may stand over a mark's plane and still be its ground (the paving's relief; a limb lying on it stands 0.12 m, ragdoll.cpp LIMB_HALF_M twice); flat_least, the least upward share of the surface's normal a blood pool lies on (0.5: no steeper than 60 degrees, so a wall's or kerb's face is left; a crater marks its own pit's walls).

lamp_pool._doc: Each lit lamp's pool of light on whatever lies under it (lamp_pool.gdshader, render/props/lamp_pools.h), added as the Roadcraft 4.0 adds its pools (scenery.ts poolMaterial): the street lights' white LED, some 4500 K, as the screen shows it (display_colour, its STREET_LED 0xffe2c4), at opacity 0.32 of it at full night, overlapping pools adding up.
